title: Forms of artificial intelligence (ai) utilization in physical education learning: a systematic literature review
text_snippet: Forms of artificial intelligence (ai) utilization in physical education learning: a systematic literature review Background. The advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed Physical Education (PE) learning into a more interactive, personalized, data-driven process. However, studies mapping AI utilization and its contributions to PE learning remain limited. Objectives. This study aimed to examine, analyze, and synthesize various forms of AI utilization in PE learning through a Systematic Literature Review (SLR). Method. The review followed PRISMA guidelines and employed the PICO framework to formulate research questions and select relevant studies. A total of 10 scientific articles were selected through purposive sampling based on predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. Data were collected through document analysis from Scopus and Google Scholar using the Publish or Perish application and analyzed through thematic synthesis. Results. The findings identified five major forms of AI utilization in PE learning: movement analysis, real-time feedback, automated assessment, AI-based learning media, and physical fitness monitoring. title: Match and compensatory training external load in professional football: A metabolic power analysis
text_snippet: Match and compensatory training external load in professional football: A metabolic power analysis Background. Compensatory training sessions (MD+1) play a critical role in football microcycle management, yet systematic comparisons with competitive match demands using metabolic power remain limited, and no such comparison has been reported in Bulgarian professional football. Objectives. The purpose of this retrospective observational pilot study was to compare the external load profiles of competitive matches and compensatory (MD+1) training sessions in a professional Bulgarian first-division football club, using average metabolic power (AMP) as the primary discriminant metric. Method. GPS data (Barin Sports PRO, 10 Hz) were retrospectively analyzed from two match–training session pairs: Match 1 (07.02.2025)/Training 1 (08.02.2025) and Match 2 (08.03.2025)/Training 2 (09.03.2025). Variables included total distance, AMP, sprint count, sprint distance, accelerations, decelerations, and top speed. Training-to-match ratios were expressed as percentages against a 50% adequacy criterion. Results. title: Motivation to play pump it up: A comparative study of adolescents and adults
text_snippet: Motivation to play pump it up: A comparative study of adolescents and adults Background. Game-based physical activity (exergaming) has emerged as an innovative approach to promoting physical activity through the integration of digital technology, music, and interactive movement. Objectives. This study examined the motivation of Pump It Up (PIU) players across adolescent and adult age groups, identified dominant motivational factors, and evaluated the potential of PIU as a technology-based exercise alternative. Method. A quantitative comparative descriptive design was employed. Data were collected using an online Likert-scale questionnaire distributed to PIU communities across Indonesia through purposive sampling. Sixty respondents participated, including 14 adolescents (11–20 years) and 46 adults (21–35 years). Data were analyzed using an Independent Samples t-test. Results. Overall motivation was high to very high, with enjoyment emerging as the strongest motivational factor (M = 4.31) in both groups. title: Trends in pedagogical approaches to the acquisition of specific movement skills: a systematic review
text_snippet: Trends in pedagogical approaches to the acquisition of specific movement skills: a systematic review Learning specific motor skills faces significant challenges due to differing goal orientations between school physical education and club performance coaching, resulting in varied efficacy of instructional methods. Therefore, this study aims to systematically identify, evaluate, and compare trends in the most effective pedagogical approaches for facilitating specific motor skill acquisition between physical education teachers and sports coaches. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, this systematic review evaluated 116 primary empirical articles (2017-2026) from six major databases. Data were analyzed thematically based on study characteristics, interventions, and motor skill outcomes. The empirical synthesis reveals distinct pedagogical tendencies with substantial overlap. In schools, teachers predominantly utilize Classroom Action Research relying on cognitive-social approaches to resolve classical movement failures. Conversely, club coaches rely on controlled experiments through repetition manipulation and tactical simulations to precisely automate athletes' discrete muscle memory. title: Optimizing sports activities on students’ mental health and motivation: a person-based framework-based mixed-methods approach
text_snippet: Optimizing sports activities on students’ mental health and motivation: a person-based framework-based mixed-methods approach Background. Mental health problems and declining academic motivation are increasingly prevalent among college students, while evidence regarding the role of physical activity in supporting psychological well-being remains limited. Objectives. This study examined the influence of physical activity on college students’ mental health and academic motivation. Method. A sequential explanatory mixed-methods design was employed. Quantitative data were collected from 199 college students using the DASS-21, Academic Motivation Scale (AMS), and Positive and Negative Affect Schedule (PANAS), followed by semi-structured interviews. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, correlation, regression, and t-tests, while qualitative data were analyzed thematically. Results. Students reported low depression, moderate anxiety and stress, and high exercise motivation. title: The effectiveness of physical fitness training on basic movement skills in supporting the habits of great indonesian children
text_snippet: The effectiveness of physical fitness training on basic movement skills in supporting the habits of great indonesian children This study examined the effectiveness of a structured physical fitness program in improving fundamental movement skills (FMS) and supporting the habits great indonesian children profile. A quasi-experimental one-group pretest-posttest design was conducted on 37 elementary school students. Data were obtained from three FMS assessments (agility running, standing long jump, target throwing) and the habits of great indonesian children questionnaire, which measures daily physical activity, healthy lifestyle, and positive character traits. Statistical analysis using SPSS version 22 included tests for normality and homogeneity, paired-sample t-tests, and effect sizes (Cohen’s d). The results showed significant improvements across all FMS domains, with large effect sizes (d = 0.70-0.95). Integrated analysis with the habits of great indonesian children revealed that most students were in the high category for daily physical activity (70%), healthy lifestyle (68%), and positive character traits (75%). title: The relationship between food intake and psychological performance in martial arts student athletes
text_snippet: The relationship between food intake and psychological performance in martial arts student athletes This study aims to determine the relationship between macronutrient intake and psychological performance in adolescent martial arts athletes. This study uses a cross-sectional method with a quantitative approach, involving student martial athletes in grades 10-12 of SMAN 10 Bandung. This study consisted of 22 male athletes and 18 female athletes. Data collection was conducted through two 24-hour food recall interviews and psychological performance questionnaires, which the athletes themselves completed. The research data were tested by Spearman’s rank bivariate analysis. The results of data collection showed that the mean of energy consumption in adolescent athletes was 1782.5 kcal; protein intake was 57.9 g; fat intake was 66.2 g; and carbohydrate intake was 191.5 g. The results showed a significant relationship (p value ≤ 0.05) between the variables of energy, protein, and carbohydrate intake with psychological performance. In contrast, fat intake was found to be unrelated to psychological performance. title: Evaluasi performa teknik batting dan bowling dalam Cricket format pendek: implikasi pemusatan latihan pada atlet remaja
text_snippet: Evaluasi performa teknik batting dan bowling dalam Cricket format pendek: implikasi pemusatan latihan pada atlet remaja Cricket format pendek menuntut efisiensi teknik dalam waktu singkat, sehingga pembinaan teknik dasar sejak usia remaja menjadi kunci dalam pengembangan atlet muda, khususnya di negara berkembang seperti Indonesia. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengevaluasi performa teknik batting dan bowling atlet Cricket remaja putra dan putri selama pemusatan latihan Cricket format pendek selama tiga bulan. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif deskriptif dengan analisis data performa dari pertandingan internal dan simulasi dalam tiga format modifikasi: T20, S8, dan S6. Sampel terdiri dari 20 atlet remaja (10 putra dan 10 putri) yang telah mengikuti minimal 80% sesi latihan. Hasil analisis menunjukkan perbedaan performa antara atlet putra dan putri, dengan atlet putra mencatat rerata run dan akurasi yang lebih tinggi. Meskipun demikian, atlet putri menunjukkan tren peningkatan yang signifikan, khususnya di kelompok pemula. text_snippet: The effect of bodyweight-based high-intensity interval training (HIIT) on VO2 max in obese adolescents The rising prevalence of adolescent obesity has become a critical health concern, particularly due to its association with impaired cardiovascular endurance and reduced VO₂ max. title: Influence of school environment on edu-physical fitness program success in 5-6 year-old children
text_snippet: Influence of school environment on edu-physical fitness program success in 5-6 year-old children The school environment plays an important role in supporting the motor development of children aged 5-6 years. Edu-Physical Fitness is a physical fitness learning approach packaged in the form of active and fun games, by the characteristics of early childhood development. This study aims to examine the influence of the school environment on the success of the implementation of the Edu-Physical Fitness program at Tunas Tridharma Plus Kindergarten Samarinda. This study uses a descriptive qualitative approach with observation techniques for the physical activity of children aged 5-6 years, in-depth interviews with four teachers, and documentation of the physical and social environmental conditions of the school. The results of the study indicate that the availability of adequate space for movement, safe and varied physical play equipment, active teacher support, and a school culture that emphasizes the importance of physical activity play a major role in increasing participation and effectiveness of the Edu-Physical Fitness program. title: Analysis of the relationship between learning achievement and mental health in special sports class student
text_snippet: Analysis of the relationship between learning achievement and mental health in special sports class student The problem in this study stems from the phenomenon of disturbed mental health among adolescents, especially special sports class students who are required to excel in academic and non-academic fields simultaneously. This pressure has the potential to affect students’ mental health, which in turn has an impact on their learning achievement. The purpose of this study was to analyze the relationship between mental health and student learning achievement in special sports classes in Semarang City. This study used a quantitative correlational approach. The sample in this study amounted to 63 students from two schools, namely SMA N 11 Semarang and SMA Sultan Agung 1 Semarang taken with total sampling technique. Mental health instruments used the DASS-21 questionnaire, while learning achievement data were obtained from even semester report cards. Data analysis was done descriptively through Kolmogorov-Smirnov normality test and Pearson correlation test with the help of IBM SPSS 27 program. title: Survey-based mapping of gross motor skills and body mass index in female students of lower grade state elementary schools
text_snippet: Survey-based mapping of gross motor skills and body mass index in female students of lower grade state elementary schools Motor skills and body mass index play an important role in carrying out daily activities, because every activity carried out requires movement. Motor skills are very important in the development stages of students for future provisions. The purpose of this study was to determine the description of gross motor skills and body mass index in female students of lower grade Elementary Schools in Blimbing District, Malang City. This study used a quantitative descriptive method with a survey design, data were collected using the Test of Gross Motor Development second edition (TGMD-2) instrument and body mass index measurements based on age (BMI/U) which were analyzed using percentage techniques. The results of data analysis from the gross motor skills test showed that lower grade female students got the average category. While the results of the body mass index measurement based on age, lower grade female students obtained normal criteria. It was concluded that female students who have gross motor skills are more physically active andhave better energy balance, which can help maintain their body mass index normal.

title: Transformations in the global sports industry: reality challenges and investment prospects - the english premier league as a model
text_snippet: Transformations in the global sports industry: reality challenges and investment prospects - the english premier league as a model The sports industry has emerged as a significant driver in the global economy and culture, often intertwined with tourism, telecommunications, and technology. The industry is growing fast but facing significant threats including global crises and digital disruption. This study takes the EPL as a case to discuss the sustainable and innovative development of the sports industry. It will consider the structure and dynamics of global sport and the world sports market and will focus on its strategic place in national development and economic stability. It is an empirical study that is conducted based on a case study approach and descriptive-analytical methods that extract best practices and pitfalls to identify challenges and opportunities. According to research, the worldwide sports market remains on a growth trajectory despite facing disruption from financial change, digital evolution, and changing consumer habits. The EPL provides evidence of how a strategic game plan, creativity and the practical application of technology empowers an organization to flourish in choppy waters. Tujuan penelitian pengembangan ini berupa mengembangkan instrumen asesmen motorik kasar anak autis berbasis video modeling. Metode yang digunakan menggunakan model developing pyschomotor test terdapat 9 langkah meliputi 1) Review criteria for a good test, 2) Analyze the sport to determine the skills or abilities to be measured, 3) Review literature, 4) Select or construct test items, 5) Determine the exact testing procedures, 6) Peer review, 7) Pilot testing, 8) Determine the statistical qualities of the test-its reliability, validity and objectivity, 9) Establish norms for norm-referenced test or determine standards for criterions-referenced tests.
